value.name: Upstream Deletion-Related ADLD

subtype_term.preferred_term: atypical adult-onset autosomal dominant demyelinating leukodystrophy

term.label: leukodystrophy, demyelinating, adult-onset, autosomal dominant, atypical

value.description: A regulatory structural-variant subtype in which heterozygous upstream deletion disrupts LMNB1 regulation without duplicating the gene. Loss of an oligodendrocyte silencer and enhancer adoption have been implicated; the requirement for ectopic enhancer activity remains unresolved. OMIM separates this as ADLDAT, and MONDO as the "atypical" child term, because the clinical picture diverges from the duplication form: onset is earlier, speech symptoms rather than dysautonomia dominate the presentation, early autonomic involvement is absent, and cerebellar and spinal-cord involvement is comparatively limited. It remains a subtype rather than a separate disease entry because both routes converge on the same proximal driver, LMNB1 overexpression.

assertion.name: Amplified and temporally altered cortical hemodynamic responses during visual stimulation on fNIRS
assertion.notes: Evidence tier: every item on this finding cites one preprint (PPR:PPR1289264), which is not peer-reviewed, so the finding is recorded as a candidate biomarker rather than an established one. The amplitude and timing components come from the same human cohort and are not independently replicated. `modifier: INCREASED` describes the amplitude component only, since the altered response timing has no direction on that axis.
assertion.context: Functional neuroimaging biomarker (functional near-infrared spectroscopy / fNIRS) for disease severity and treatment response monitoring; not an established diagnostic criterion but demonstrates translational value as a cross-species biomarker of AS-specific cortical dysfunction.
assertion.description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) during visual stimulation reveals amplified and temporally altered hemodynamic responses in individuals with AS compared to controls. In the human arm these alterations are consistently detected across preprocessing strategies and stable across age; sensitivity to therapeutic UBE3A restoration has been shown only in the mouse, not in the human cohort. The finding is conserved across species: AS mouse models exhibit enhanced visual cortical responses on intrinsic optical signal imaging that persist across development, scale with disease severity, and normalize with UBE3A restoration.

selected_evidence.snippet: restoration of UBE3A expression normalizes visual responses and scales with both behavioral recovery and molecular rescue.
